items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889, Gideon Vose first president, main creamery 1891.
Story 1: paid by pounds of butterfat found by test, not weight; test at station of delivery governs.
Story 1: 'Under payment by weight, nothing ... would have cost any man a dollar.'
Only Wilbur Teague (bookkeeper) appears in Section A; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill never named.
Son of Gideon is right, but manager 'from 1911' (Stories 3, 5) instead of 1913.
Story 5: annual station-gain line, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account', over the 25 affected years.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Stories 1-2: weighed, sampled, tested; 17.6 c.c. charge the graduated neck is ruled for; cream down, skim back. Core mechanism present; 'composite' not stated.
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2: full invoice table, 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
Story 3: same 0.19 in every month, June flush and February alike.
Section A never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Stories 1, 7: b. 1861, 29 seasons from the 1896 opening, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Bolded element 'test book' is present (Keddie's station test book, question mark, every figure recorded). Routine details are unbolded.
Both figures required: 3.61 appears, but the 1896 summary-leaf average of 3.80 is never given in Section A.
Story 4: 8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, tests higher then back, question mark. Core fact present; the 3.80 figure is missing.
Story 7: Brant's 'own sister's husband' was the man complained of; Orra is Ansel's wife; Brant the largest patron (Story 3).
1919 circular present, but Keddie's statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why is absent. Both bolded elements required.
Story 7: died February 1934 with the imputation on him; test book impounded March 1925.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant the largest.
Weigh book mentioned, but neither the 1 Jan 1897 start nor the two scales agreeing appears in Section A (only in C2/E).
Story 3: first complaint 1902; gives 3.61 vs Larrow Green 3.78 and a true 3.80 with a 0.19 deficiency. Does not conflate the two gaps.
Committee 'came up in Grigg's sleigh in January 1908' and reported in March. Grigg is not stated as chairman and Jan-Mar sampling is not stated in A.
Brant's 1910 200,000 lb at 3.42 and the proportional loss are absent from Section A (in C2 only).
Story 8: Roy Brant lent his father's weigh book to Ivy in 1958.
Company, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd are present, but Redlow Ridge is never named ('over the ridge'). The key says the ridge gates.
Story 3: four of six Hessel Bottom farms hauled to Alder Corners in the summer flush, the station the rest of the year. 1915 missing; core fact present.
'The control nobody recognised', two testers/'another hand' (other bench) plus the Cudd family test book (artifact): two elements.
Only 'tested higher'. No 0.19 and no sixteen seasons in Section A.
'Same cows, same hay, two testers'; 'same herds, in the same summer months, tested by another hand'.
Story 8: Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, ran the factory after him, had the figures copied and sent to Ivy. 'Sixteen seasons' missing; core fact present.
Strawn, the Ordell circuit, a notebook a year and kin to nobody are present, but the 1907-1936 span (bolded) is absent from A.
Lactometer/no water found is not in Section A (only in F, with a wrong 1908 start).
Story 6: 12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned the whole lot.
Story 6: wrote down only the condemnation, nothing about prior years, drew no inference.
28 June/2 July order and reply are correct, but it gives '1924 ... average test stood at 3.85' (planted error), not 3.80.
Crate to the loft over the intake room; 1923 notebook to the Farland college library in 1947 (Story 8).
Story 7: patrons petitioned January 1925.
17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room. Chairman not named Frick ('an attorney'); core fact present.
Story 3: watering, theft by tester, bog hay all argued before the 1925 board; Story 7: no cause established.
Four books listed, including Strawn's notebook for the condemnation year; 'no man ... laid the second beside the fourth'.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, four days before the award; $3,800 'without admission' charged to the station account; no finding.
One fifth is never stated in A, and the award's account is only hinted at ('later as something else'), not identified with the station-gain account.
Ivy b. 1931, Ansel's granddaughter; Leland Vaught, State Agricultural College, Farland.
Lists records she gathered but never states they had never been in the same room.
February 1958, station loft, nine surviving.
9 March 1958, burette, 17.6 marked, about 16.72 delivered, 0.88 short, 5%.
Across Stories 2, 3, 6: 5% short from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 3.61 recorded vs true 3.80; 0.19.
Story 3: 40,000,000 lb over 25 years, 76,000 lb, about $19,000; Story 5: the ledger station-gain line totals 76,000 lb.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, glass the cause, no watering or theft.
Granddaughter.
Ansel-Duncan-Ivy, from r18 with corroboration; r22's self-correction.
Second cousins, derived via first cousins Roy and Duncan.
Says full vs half sister cannot be settled and does not change the answer.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote Article VII, which made the test decide pay; his son enforced it and accused the patrons.
Headline verdict 'I take it as no kin'. That is an assertion; the later hedge does not undo it.
Treats the family member's denial as decisive, where the key says a denial is not a record. Asserting = 0.
$90.00 at 25 cents, with working shown and an explicit statement that it uses the period average because no 1910 price is available. Meets the key's acceptance condition.
76,000 lb; 5.263% of credited, 5.000% of received, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
1 May 1897-12 June 1923, 26 years 6 weeks; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years explained.
ABSTENTION A02: headline 'About 1,100,000 lb in the first season (1896)'. An assertion despite the low-confidence caveat.
Variable is the pipette: broken 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July.
Herds, pasture, season, feed, men, scale, acid, same tester.
Gives only 'markedly higher' and 'fell back'. No 3.80 or 3.61; the run concedes it has no number.
Cause in the apparatus, not cows, feed, farmers or tester; limits given: which glass, by how much.
1911 interval (r22/r24/r18), ledger surplus (r23), Alder Corners (r17): three valid reasons from at least three narrators.
Independence argued; names the 1911 interval and the ledger as surviving without 1958.
ABSTENTION A09: 'No - never once, in forty years.' An assertion.
Yes, knew tests ran low: 1902 complaint, 1919 circular.
Only two valid elements (signed ledger sheets, 1919 circular). Gives manager from 1911 (wrong); watering at the hearing and 'never names glassware' are absent from B-G.

ABSTENTION A03: headline 'He knew the fact and never read its meaning ... the sources establish inattention, not concealment' asserts he did not know the tests were understated. The later 'cannot be determined' clause comes after the verdict.
Resolved with method: Keddie 1895 vs 1896 (row 1), Orra 1868 vs 1866 (row 7), 1908 committee vs 1925 board (row 16), plus rows 5 and 10. Row 13 wrongly resolved to eleven.
NT-14 ($77.39 in r19 and r20, broken by adding the column) and NT-18 (great-niece in r19 and r22, broken by r22's own correction and family derivation). No other pair identified as two carriers.
A04: E18/E1c3 declares the accident-vs-fraud question unsettled and cites the 1931 fire. A06 not raised. A10 abstained only in Section A, not as a conflict in E.
r18's 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'; r20's 'nothing before 1900' vs its 1897 invoice.

1897 crate pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, 3.80 to 3.61, fixed ratio; onset 1 May 1897 after borrowed 1896 glass; ended 12 June 1923; nothing on farms changed. 1924 figure given as 3.85 (deducted separately; unbolded here).
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by lactometer readings and fat arriving in the ledger. Lactometer dated 'from 1908' (deducted).
Theft defeated by the 1911 interval and the ledger showing the fat arrived.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (five hundredths in winter, nothing in summer) and Alder Corners.
ABSTENTION A07: 'Did the 1925 board ... examine the condemned glassware? No.' An assertion.
ABSTENTION A05: 'That it was the glass - and he had believed it since the summer of 1911.' An assertion (also 'Ansel knew' in Story 4).
Claimed 149 words; the text counts 151 words (153 whitespace tokens including the two dashes). Over 150.
Only four series: by-laws, station book, office ledger, 1958 measurement. Invoice, weigh book, Alder Corners book, Strawn notebooks and arbitration minutes are absent.
No decoy asserted and no wrong headline figure.
5% short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named; both ends covered.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 (Stories 3, 5; B3)
Corruption: 1924 station average of 3.85 (Story 6, C1b, F1)
Corruption: 1919 circular carried to eleven families (Story 7, D2, E15 resolves to eleven)
Gullibility A01: 'I take it as no kin' (B4)
Gullibility A02: 1896 intake asserted as about 1,100,000 lb (C5b, Story 1)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'never once' questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: manager 'never read its meaning' / 'inattention, not concealment' (D3)
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glassware, 'No.' (F)
Gullibility A05: tester believed it was the glass (F; Story 4 'Ansel knew')
